$comment: CPE-1594 ratchet, made CASE-granular by CPE-1677. Each entry is ONE test case (`spec` = the spec file's basename, `test` = the it() title, verbatim) that is ALLOWED to fail today. Any OTHER case failing reds the job — including a case inside a spec file that already has entries here, which is exactly the hole CPE-1677 closed (whole-file exemptions meant the other 24 cases in samples.smoke.ts guarded nothing). Removing an entry is one-way: once a listed case passes, the ratchet FAILS until its entry is deleted. A listed `test` that matches NO case in the run also FAILS (titles drift; a rename must not silently drop both the exemption and the coverage). Entries are exact titles, never patterns — a pattern would re-create the blanket exemption this replaced. An entry with "intermittent": true is a case PROVEN to both pass and fail on unchanged code (cite the runs in its reason): it is exempt in both directions, because a coin-flip case would otherwise red every run one way or the other — but it must still exist, and the ratchet prints it with its observed status on every run so it stays visible until it is fixed and deleted. See gui-smoke/README.md 'The ratchet' for the retire procedure.

Left listed pending a WebKitGTK-specific investigation.

cases.test: opens the Trash from the Sidebar and selects the real, natively-seeded deleted entry
cases.reason: ENVIRONMENTAL, not a code defect in the spec or in TrashView.svelte's titlebar fix (CPE-1827): clicking the Sidebar's Open-Trash row never returned a WebDriver result and the session log showed 'Timed out receiving message from renderer' — the CPE-1827 Foreman confirmed this is the known msedgedriver-150-vs-Edge-151 version mismatch already reproduced on the repo's OWN STOCK open-dir.smoke.ts (tracked in .claude/qa-architecture/MANUAL-TEST-BURNDOWN.md), not anything specific to this spec or to `list_trash_stream`. A separate, real observation from the same debugging session — this dev machine's actual Recycle Bin held 843 items (Shell.Application COM probe) which could independently slow `list_trash_stream` — is filed as its own PR-body note, not the cause recorded here; which of the two dominates was not determined. Expected to clear automatically the moment a clean CI run (matched driver/browser versions) proves this case passing — the ratchet forces this entry's removal at that point, not a manual retire. See CPE-1822 (owns full Trash gui-smoke coverage) for anything beyond the driver-mismatch fix itself.
